audit.whatIsWrong: The page called this FAVOURED at 4/10 and the prose called it 'one of the most lopsided lanes in your favor'. Cassiopeia wins 45.47% of 1192 games here.
audit.why: Naafiri's Darkin Daggers reach 900 to Cassiopeia's 850 Noxious Blast and 700 Twin Fang, each dagger bleeds, and packmates add damage to every one. Cassiopeia has no dash and Hounds' Pursuit is a lock-on. She loses the lane and wins the scaling.
audit.corrected: TRICKY, 6.5/10, Naafiri carry threat 7/10 — survive the early bleed, win at two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Cassiopeia 7/7 stages — packet.defects flags this directly against a 45.47% win rate.
audit.why: Naafiri owns levels 1-6 on range, packmate damage and Eviscerate's 7s-at-rank-5 reset; Cassiopeia's spike is Seraph's/Liandry's (parity) and then full build (hers).
audit.corrected: Naafiri 1, 2, 3, 4-5, 6; Skill at first item; Cassiopeia at two-plus items. Proposed as paired phases[N].side + win[N] edits with every why and whys[] rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never named a single Naafiri ability (packet.defects flags it) and content spikes[1] invented 'Hound Squad' for her ultimate.
audit.why: Real names and numbers: We Are More (P) packmates, Darkin Daggers (Q) 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s at 900, The Call of the Pack (W) untargetable on 26/24/22/20/18s, Eviscerate (E) 450 dash that damages, recalls and fully heals the pack on 11/10/9/8/7s, Hounds' Pursuit (R) 110/95/80s lock-on dash that reveals on takedown and shields on the recast. Miasma grounds Q's leap, E and R; Petrifying Gaze stuns only enemies facing her, which her R landing satisfies. She can go untargetable through a commit (W, E, R) and she heals through chip damage, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Named every ability with its real cooldown, stated the grounding-vs-dash and facing-vs-stun interactions, and added the untargetability and anti-heal points.

audit.why: It is the field that exists to carry real numbers.
audit.corrected: Hounds' Pursuit 110/95/80s, Eviscerate 11/10/9/8/7s, Darkin Daggers 9s at rank 1, Miasma 24/22/20/18/16s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal was mentioned only as 'his sustain' with no mechanism.
audit.why: Eviscerate fully heals her packmates on a 7s cooldown at rank 5, so chip damage is undone between trades.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds is a timing item here, not a situational one.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string, both pasted under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2), plus seven misgendered fields.

audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to their own titles; every he/his replaced.

edits.before: Naafiri has almost no way to reach you safely — she has to walk through your Noxious Blast and Twin Fang poke just to get in range, and her Pack dogs die instantly to a well-placed Miasma. This is one of the most lopsided lanes in your favor: as long as you don't walk into a jungler gank, you should be poking her to nothing by level 5 without ever taking a real risk yourself.
edits.after: Naafiri reaches you fine: Darkin Daggers travel 900 to your 850 Noxious Blast, each dagger bleeds, and her packmates add damage to every one she lands. Your job in the first five levels is not to bully her — it is to farm, dodge the second dagger, and stack Tear. Keep Miasma up for Eviscerate: it dashes 450, damages around her, and fully heals the pack, so a chase past your own poison zone just hands her a free reset.

edits.before: Level 6 gives her Hound Squad for a flashier all-in, but Petrifying Gaze punishes the commitment hard — the instant she dashes in, you stun and delete her before the dogs matter. Keep playing the poke game and force her to either give up CS or die trying to close the gap; there's no good option for her here.
edits.after: Level 6 hands her Hounds' Pursuit: a 110s lock-on dash that cannot be dodged and shields on the recast. Petrifying Gaze answers it only if you are facing her when she lands, so hold the R for that instant, not for poke. Between R cooldowns the lane is a farm race — take the safe CS, keep Miasma for Eviscerate, and let your item timings do the work.

edits.before: Rylai's shuts her engage down completely since the slow keeps her at poke range permanently, and Void Staff with full poison stacks means anything she manages to land still isn't enough to kill you first. Full-build Cassiopeia simply wins every stage of this matchup — group fights, skirmishes, and 1v1s alike — as her all-in kit has no answer to being kept at range.
edits.after: Rylai's slow with Miasma grounding is what finally stops Eviscerate resetting the trade, and Void Staff plus stacked poison brings your damage past what her burst and the Hounds' Pursuit shield can cover. This is where the matchup turns: ground their engage, petrify whoever jumps you, and Naafiri has to fight you on your terms instead of on hers.

notes: This page was the worst of my slice: a 45.47% matchup over 1192 games written as a stomp, a 7/7 level chart in both layers, not one Naafiri ability named anywhere, and a fabricated ultimate name ('Hound Squad') in content spikes[1]. I moved the chart to Naafiri levels 1-6, Skill at first item, Cassiopeia at two-plus, with every phases[].side paired to its win[N] and every why and whys[] rewritten in the same proposal. phases[6] keeps Cassiopeia so no win[6] pair was needed. I did not touch report[13].t or report[3].t even though they duplicate ahead/tradeGood, to stay inside the report cap; they will now differ slightly from the fields they mirror. Rylai's appears in the content layer while the full layer's itemization says Seraph's into Liandry's into Rabadon's — the same build contradiction I flagged on mel, unresolved across the champion.
